meta.name: Explain pasted code and follow-up questions with GPT-4.1 and Slack

name: Explain pasted code and follow-up questions with OpenAI GPT-4.1 and Slack

parameters.content:
## Code Explainer — Tool-Calling Agent, Audience Levels & Security Escalation

This is NOT the linear 'analyze -> explain -> wait -> approve -> send' pipeline. Here the LLM is a real function-calling AGENT that decides for itself when to run static analysis (via a tool, not a fixed pre-step), the explanation depth is chosen by a genuine 3-way SWITCH with swappable customization nodes, follow-up questions are handled through session MEMORY across separate calls (no pause-and-resume loop needed), and the single Wait node only fires conditionally — when the agent itself flags a security concern — rather than gating every response behind a blanket approval step. Delivery is a SWITCH to whichever optional destination node you've wired up (Slack, Discord, or a plain webhook response), so you can delete the two you don't need.

### How it works
1. Webhook - Code Submitted receives the code, an optional audienceLevel ('beginner'/'intermediate'/'expert'), an optional sessionId (for follow-up continuity) and an outputChannel preference
2. Switch - Audience Level routes to one of three small, independently editable Set nodes that each define a different explanationStyle instruction — these are the 'floating' customization nodes: duplicate, edit or remove them freely without touching the rest of the flow
3. AI Agent - Code Explainer (GPT-4.1-mini + session-keyed memory) is given a tool, Tool - Analyze Code Structure, and decides on its own to call it for objective metrics (language, line counts, functions, rough complexity) before writing an explanation at the requested depth. Because memory is session-keyed, a follow-up question sent later with the same sessionId is answered in context automatically — no explicit pause/resume node needed for that
4. Set - Parse Agent Output extracts the agent's structured JSON
5. IF - Security Concern Flagged only pauses the flow (Wait - For Expert Security Review) when the agent itself has flagged something worth a human look (hardcoded secrets, injection risk, missing auth, etc.) — everything else goes straight through
6. Switch - Output Channel fans out to whichever delivery node matches outputChannel; Slack and Discord are optional/floating — keep the one you use, delete the other

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add an OpenAI (or compatible) credential on the OpenAI Chat Model
3. Add Slack and/or Discord credentials only on the delivery node(s) you plan to keep
4. Point Wait - For Expert Security Review's resume webhook at your reviewer UI's 'approve/block' action
5. POST code (plus audienceLevel/outputChannel/sessionId) to the webhook to test; send a second request with the same sessionId and no code, just a question, to test follow-up memory

## 1. Trigger, Audience Switch & Tool-Calling Agent

- **Webhook - Code Submitted** — receives the code, audience level, session ID, and output channel preference.
- **Set - Config** — extracts code, focus question, audience level, session ID, and channel settings from the request.
- **Switch - Audience Level** — routes to the matching explanation-style branch (beginner/intermediate/expert).
- **Set - Beginner Explanation Style** — defines plain-language, jargon-free explanation instructions.
- **Set - Expert Explanation Style** — defines concise, technical explanation instructions for experienced engineers.
- **Set - Intermediate Explanation Style** — defines explanation instructions assuming general programming fundamentals.
- **Tool - Analyze Code Structure** — callable tool the agent can invoke for objective code metrics (language, line counts, complexity).
- **OpenAI Chat Model** — the LLM powering the agent. 🔑
- **Window Buffer Memory** — session-keyed memory so follow-up questions are answered in context.
- **AI Agent - Code Explainer** — decides whether to call the analysis tool, then writes the explanation and flags security concerns.

## 2. Conditional Escalation (not a blanket gate)

- **Set - Parse Agent Output** — extracts the agent's structured JSON output.
- **IF - Security Concern Flagged** — branches to human review only when the agent itself flagged a security issue.
- **Wait - For Expert Security Review** — pauses for a reviewer to approve or block flagged code.
- **IF - Review Approved** — gates delivery on the reviewer's decision.
- **Respond to Webhook - Blocked** — returns a "blocked, needs manual follow-up" response when not approved.

## 3. Optional/Floating Delivery Destinations

- **Switch - Output Channel** — routes to the requested delivery destination (Slack, Discord, or webhook response).
- **Slack - Send Code Explanation (optional)** — posts the explanation to Slack; optional, wire up only if used. 🔑
- **Discord - Send Code Explanation (optional)** — posts the explanation to Discord; optional, wire up only if used. 🔑
- **Respond to Webhook - Return Explanation** — returns the explanation directly as the HTTP response.

assignments.name: explanationStyle
assignments.value: Explain in plain, jargon-free language as if teaching someone brand new to programming. Define every technical term the first time you use it, and lean on everyday analogies.

assignments.name: explanationStyle
assignments.value: Be concise and technical. Skip basic language mechanics and focus on non-obvious behavior, edge cases, algorithmic complexity, and idiomatic alternatives an experienced engineer would want to know.

assignments.name: explanationStyle
assignments.value: Assume solid general programming fundamentals but limited familiarity with this specific language or library. Use precise technical terms, each briefly defined on first use.

parameters.name: analyze_code_structure
parameters.description: Analyzes a code snippet and returns objective metrics as JSON: detected language, total/code/comment/blank line counts, detected function/method names, and a rough cyclomatic-complexity estimate. Call this with the exact code before writing your explanation — do not guess these numbers.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'blocked', message: 'This code flagged a security concern and was not approved for automatic explanation delivery. A reviewer will follow up directly.', securityDetails: $json.parsedOutput.securityDetails }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ sessionId: $json.sessionId, summary: $json.parsedOutput.summary, lineByLine: $json.parsedOutput.lineByLine, complexityAnalysis: $json.parsedOutput.complexityAnalysis, potentialIssues: $json.parsedOutput.potentialIssues, suggestions: $json.parsedOutput.suggestions }) }}
